title: The riddle of two guards
description: Two doors stand before you, each watched by a guard. One door leads to safety. One guard always tells the truth; the other always lies. You do not know which is which. Together with your inner companion, find a way through.
facts: Exactly one of the two doors leads to safety.
Exactly one guard always tells the truth; the other always lies.
Both guards know which door is safe and how the other guard answers.
You may ask one guard a single yes-or-no question.
goal: Find a question whose answer identifies both doors and a strategy that always chooses the safe door, whichever guard you ask.
source_text:
theory Riddle_of_Two_Guards
  imports Main
begin

(* There are two doors, each with a guard stood in front,
   one is a truth-teller, the other is a liar,
   and only one of the doors leads to safety. *)

datatype position =
    Left
  | Right

fun other_position :: "position \<Rightarrow> position" where
  "other_position Left = Right"
| "other_position Right = Left"

datatype guard =
    TruthTeller
  | Liar

fun other_guard :: "guard \<Rightarrow> guard" where
  "other_guard TruthTeller = Liar"
| "other_guard Liar = TruthTeller"

datatype door =
    Safe
  | Unsafe

definition other_door :: "position \<Rightarrow> position" where
  "other_door = other_position"

record world =
  door_at :: "position \<Rightarrow> door"
  guard_at :: "position \<Rightarrow> guard"

definition valid_world :: "world \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "valid_world w \<longleftrightarrow>
      door_at w Left \<noteq> door_at w Right
    \<and> guard_at w Left \<noteq> guard_at w Right"

definition door_is_safe :: "world \<Rightarrow> position \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "door_is_safe w p \<longleftrightarrow> door_at w p = Safe"


(* You are allowed to ask one guard a single yes-or-no question. *)

(* A truth-teller answers honestly.
   A liar will always answer the opposite. *)

fun answers :: "guard \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "answers TruthTeller p = p"
| "answers Liar p = (\<not> p)"

end

theory Fictional_Forensic_Murder_Investigation
  imports Main
begin

(* ====================================================== *)
(* Problem Statement and Definitions                      *)
(* ====================================================== *)

(*
  Fictional case:

  Victim: Dr. Gray

  Suspects:
    - Alice
    - Brian
    - Clara

  Investigators discover:
    1. Clara's fingerprints are on the murder weapon.
    2. Clara's DNA is present at the crime scene.
    3. Clara has no verified alibi.
    4. Alice and Brian both have verified alibis.

  Investigative rule (fictional):
    A suspect is considered the culprit if they have
    fingerprints on the weapon, DNA at the scene,
    and lack a verified alibi.
*)

datatype person =
    Alice
  | Brian
  | Clara

consts
  fingerprints_on_weapon :: "person \<Rightarrow> bool"
  dna_at_scene :: "person \<Rightarrow> bool"
  verified_alibi :: "person \<Rightarrow> bool"

definition culprit :: "person \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "culprit p \<longleftrightarrow>
      fingerprints_on_weapon p \<and>
      dna_at_scene p \<and>
      \<not> verified_alibi p"

locale Fictional_Case =
  assumes
    clara_fingerprints:
      "fingerprints_on_weapon Clara"
  and
    clara_dna:
      "dna_at_scene Clara"
  and
    clara_no_alibi:
      "\<not> verified_alibi Clara"
  and
    alice_alibi:
      "verified_alibi Alice"
  and
    brian_alibi:
      "verified_alibi Brian"

begin

(* ====================================================== *)

end
end

title: Murder investigation · The missing minutes
description: I am reviewing the fictional death of Dr Vale. Morgan Reed, Casey Lowe and Jordan Pike give different accounts. I must separate recorded evidence, accepted findings, and the case's rules for an outcome.
goal: Establish the permitted outcome for Morgan, Casey and Jordan under the case's stated rules.
facts: The incident window consists of 21:10, 21:15 and 21:20. A verified alibi requires reliable coverage and accepted presence throughout that window.

Morgan claims the library. An admissible, reliable, independent library log supports presence at 21:00 only. Morgan's corridor presence at 21:10 is accepted, and no verified alibi is an explicit case assumption.
Casey claims the bus; Jordan claims the hospital. Each has admissible, reliable, independent CCTV support and accepted presence at all three incident times.
For Morgan, causation, required intent and unlawfulness are accepted. All seven listed innocent alternatives are explicitly excluded.
Causation is explicitly not accepted for Casey or Jordan. Handling a weapon is not by itself an accepted finding of causing death.
Conviction requires proved offence elements, temporal capability and excluded relevant alternatives; acquittal is required otherwise in this fictional model.

theory Temporal_Multi_Suspect_Forensic_Investigation
  imports Main
begin

(* ============================================================ *)
(* Problem statement and definitions                            *)
(* ============================================================ *)

(*
  Entirely fictional case: The death of Dr Rowan Vale.

  The relevant incident window is reconstructed as lying between
  21:10 and 21:20.

  Suspects:

    Morgan Reed:
      Allegedly seen near the scene during the incident window.
      Claims to have been at the Northbridge Library.

    Casey Lowe:
      Had earlier contact with the victim.
      Claims to have been travelling on a bus.

    Jordan Pike:
      Was initially treated as a suspect.
      Claims to have been working at a hospital.

  The model distinguishes:

    - a person merely stating an alibi;
    - evidence supporting an alibi;
    - the reliability and independence of that evidence;
    - an alibi covering the complete possible incident window;
    - forensic source inv_propositions;
    - activity-level inv_propositions;
    - offence elements;
    - the fact-finder's final assessment.

  Time is represented discretely. This is a small temporal model,
  rather than a full continuous-time reconstruction.
*)

datatype person =
    Dr_Vale
  | Morgan_Reed
  | Casey_Lowe
  | Jordan_Pike
  | Unknown_Person

datatype timepoint =
    T2050
  | T2100
  | T2105
  | T2110
  | T2115
  | T2120
  | T2125
  | T2130
  | T2140
  | T2150
  | T2200

datatype location =
    Vale_Office
  | Office_Corridor
  | Northbridge_Library
  | Number_47_Bus
  | Central_Hospital
  | Unknown_Location

datatype exhibit =
    Knife_DNA
  | Knife_Fingerprint
  | Corridor_CCTV
  | Library_Access_Log
  | Library_CCTV
  | Bus_Ticket_Record
  | Bus_CCTV
  | Hospital_Access_Log
  | Hospital_CCTV
  | Phone_Location_Data
  | Bloodstained_Jacket
  | Post_Mortem_Report

datatype inv_proposition =
    Morgan_Handled_Knife
  | Casey_Handled_Knife
  | Jordan_Handled_Knife
  | Morgan_Was_In_Corridor
  | Casey_Was_On_Bus
  | Jordan_Was_At_Hospital
  | Morgan_Wore_Jacket
  | Victim_Blood_On_Jacket
  | Fatal_Injury_Occurred
  | Morgan_Caused_Fatal_Injury
  | Casey_Caused_Fatal_Injury
  | Jordan_Caused_Fatal_Injury
  | Morgan_Intended_Death_Or_Serious_Injury
  | Casey_Intended_Death_Or_Serious_Injury
  | Jordan_Intended_Death_Or_Serious_Injury
  | Morgan_Acted_Unlawfully
  | Casey_Acted_Unlawfully
  | Jordan_Acted_Unlawfully

datatype alternative =
    Earlier_Innocent_Handling
  | Secondary_DNA_Transfer
  | Laboratory_Contamination
  | CCTV_Misidentification
  | Device_Not_Carried_By_Owner
  | Alibi_Record_Error
  | Unknown_Third_Party_Responsible

(*
  The prosecution does not know the exact instant of the fatal injury.

  Instead, post-mortem and other temporal evidence define a possible
  incident window.
*)

definition incident_window :: "timepoint \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "incident_window t \<longleftrightarrow>
      t = T2110 \<or>
      t = T2115 \<or>
      t = T2120"

definition before_incident_window :: "timepoint \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "before_incident_window t \<longleftrightarrow>
      t = T2050 \<or>
      t = T2100 \<or>
      t = T2105"

definition after_incident_window :: "timepoint \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "after_incident_window t \<longleftrightarrow>
      t = T2125 \<or>
      t = T2130 \<or>
      t = T2140 \<or>
      t = T2150 \<or>
      t = T2200"

(*
  A reconstruction may place a person at a particular location
  at a particular time.

  This relation represents an accepted temporal finding. It is not
  generated automatically merely because an electronic record exists.
*)

consts
  accepted_location :: "person \<Rightarrow> timepoint \<Rightarrow> location \<Rightarrow> bool"

definition at_scene :: "person \<Rightarrow> timepoint \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "at_scene p t \<longleftrightarrow>
      accepted_location p t Vale_Office \<or>
      accepted_location p t Office_Corridor"

definition present_during_window :: "person \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "present_during_window p \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<exists>t. incident_window t \<and> at_scene p t)"

definition away_throughout_window :: "person \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "away_throughout_window p \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall>t. incident_window t \<longrightarrow> \<not> at_scene p t)"

(*
  Presence during one part of the incident window does not by itself
  prove presence at the unknown instant of the fatal act.

  Similarly, being absent at one minute does not establish an alibi
  unless the absence covers the complete possible incident window.
*)

definition continuously_at_location_during_window ::
  "person \<Rightarrow> location \<Rightarrow> bool"
where
  "continuously_at_location_during_window p l \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall>t. incident_window t \<longrightarrow> accepted_location p t l)"

(* ---------- Alibi structure ---------- *)

(*
  A claimed alibi is only an account provided by or for the suspect.
  It is not necessarily true, complete, independent, or reliable.
*)

consts
  claims_alibi :: "person \<Rightarrow> location \<Rightarrow> bool"
  alibi_supports_presence ::
    "exhibit \<Rightarrow> person \<Rightarrow> timepoint \<Rightarrow> location \<Rightarrow> bool"
  alibi_exhibit_reliable :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool"
  alibi_exhibit_independent :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool"
  alibi_exhibit_admissible :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool"

definition reliable_alibi_support ::
  "exhibit \<Rightarrow> person \<Rightarrow> timepoint \<Rightarrow> location \<Rightarrow> bool"
where
  "reliable_alibi_support e p t l \<longleftrightarrow>
      alibi_exhibit_admissible e \<and>
      alibi_exhibit_reliable e \<and>
      alibi_exhibit_independent e \<and>
      alibi_supports_presence e p t l"

(*
  One reliable data point does not necessarily cover the whole window.

  A complete evidential alibi requires reliable and independent
  support for every possible incident time.
*)

definition exhibit_covers_complete_window ::
  "exhibit \<Rightarrow> person \<Rightarrow> location \<Rightarrow> bool"
where
  "exhibit_covers_complete_window e p l \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall>t. incident_window t \<longrightarrow> reliable_alibi_support e p t l)"

(*
  Some real alibis depend on several exhibits considered together.
  The following definition allows a different reliable exhibit to
  support each time in the incident window.
*)

definition combined_evidence_covers_window ::
  "person \<Rightarrow> location \<Rightarrow> bool"
where
  "combined_evidence_covers_window p l \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall>t. incident_window t \<longrightarrow>
        (\<exists>e. reliable_alibi_support e p t l))"

(*
  A verified alibi additionally requires the fact-finder to accept
  that the person was continuously at the claimed alternative
  location.

  Requiring both evidential coverage and an accepted location finding
  avoids defining an alibi solely by the existence of a database entry.
*)

definition verified_alibi_at :: "person \<Rightarrow> location \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "verified_alibi_at p l \<longleftrightarrow>
      claims_alibi p l \<and>
      combined_evidence_covers_window p l \<and>
      continuously_at_location_during_window p l"

definition has_verified_alibi :: "person \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "has_verified_alibi p \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<exists>l. l \<noteq> Vale_Office \<and>
           l \<noteq> Office_Corridor \<and>
           verified_alibi_at p l)"

(* ---------- Forensic integrity and admissibility ---------- *)

consts
  collected_lawfully :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool"
  continuity_preserved :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool"
  method_validated :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool"
  quality_controls_passed :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool"
  examiner_competent :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool"
  limitations_disclosed :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool"
  relevant :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool"
  excluded_by_court :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool"

definition forensic_integrity :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "forensic_integrity e \<longleftrightarrow>
      continuity_preserved e \<and>
      method_validated e \<and>
      quality_controls_passed e \<and>
      examiner_competent e \<and>
      limitations_disclosed e"

definition admissible :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "admissible e \<longleftrightarrow>
      collected_lawfully e \<and>
      relevant e \<and>
      forensic_integrity e \<and>
      \<not> excluded_by_court e"

(* ---------- Evidential inv_propositions ---------- *)

consts
  supports :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> inv_proposition \<Rightarrow> bool"
  strongly_supports :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> inv_proposition \<Rightarrow> bool"
  consistent_with :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> alternative \<Rightarrow> bool"

definition usable_support :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> inv_proposition \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "usable_support e p \<longleftrightarrow>
      admissible e \<and> supports e p"

definition usable_strong_support :: "exhibit \<Rightarrow> inv_proposition \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "usable_strong_support e p \<longleftrightarrow>
      admissible e \<and> strongly_supports e p"

(*
  Temporal corroboration requires evidence supporting presence
  at a particular location and time. The exact weight remains for
  the fact-finder.
*)

consts
  temporally_supports ::
    "exhibit \<Rightarrow> person \<Rightarrow> timepoint \<Rightarrow> location \<Rightarrow> bool"

definition usable_temporal_support ::
  "exhibit \<Rightarrow> person \<Rightarrow> timepoint \<Rightarrow> location \<Rightarrow> bool"
where
  "usable_temporal_support e p t l \<longleftrightarrow>
      admissible e \<and> temporally_supports e p t l"

(* ---------- Charge-specific legal findings ---------- *)

(*
  The case against each suspect is assessed separately.

  Evidence against Morgan cannot automatically count against Casey
  or Jordan.
*)

consts
  fact_finder_accepts :: "inv_proposition \<Rightarrow> bool"
  realistic_possibility :: "alternative \<Rightarrow> bool"

definition morgan_elements_proved :: bool where
  "morgan_elements_proved \<longleftrightarrow>
      fact_finder_accepts Morgan_Caused_Fatal_Injury \<and>
      fact_finder_accepts Morgan_Intended_Death_Or_Serious_Injury \<and>
      fact_finder_accepts Morgan_Acted_Unlawfully"

definition casey_elements_proved :: bool where
  "casey_elements_proved \<longleftrightarrow>
      fact_finder_accepts Casey_Caused_Fatal_Injury \<and>
      fact_finder_accepts Casey_Intended_Death_Or_Serious_Injury \<and>
      fact_finder_accepts Casey_Acted_Unlawfully"

definition jordan_elements_proved :: bool where
  "jordan_elements_proved \<longleftrightarrow>
      fact_finder_accepts Jordan_Caused_Fatal_Injury \<and>
      fact_finder_accepts Jordan_Intended_Death_Or_Serious_Injury \<and>
      fact_finder_accepts Jordan_Acted_Unlawfully"

(*
  An intact verified alibi prevents a finding of guilt in this
  simplified model.

  This is intentionally stronger and cleaner than many real cases,
  where the scope and implications of an alibi may be disputed.
*)

definition temporally_capable :: "person \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "temporally_capable p \<longleftrightarrow>
      present_during_window p \<and> \<not> has_verified_alibi p"

definition relevant_alternatives_excluded :: bool where
  "relevant_alternatives_excluded \<longleftrightarrow>
      \<not> realistic_possibility Earlier_Innocent_Handling \<and>
      \<not> realistic_possibility Secondary_DNA_Transfer \<and>
      \<not> realistic_possibility Laboratory_Contamination \<and>
      \<not> realistic_possibility CCTV_Misidentification \<and>
      \<not> realistic_possibility Device_Not_Carried_By_Owner \<and>
      \<not> realistic_possibility Alibi_Record_Error \<and>
      \<not> realistic_possibility Unknown_Third_Party_Responsible"

definition sure_morgan_guilty :: bool where
  "sure_morgan_guilty \<longleftrightarrow>
      morgan_elements_proved \<and>
      temporally_capable Morgan_Reed \<and>
      relevant_alternatives_excluded"

definition sure_casey_guilty :: bool where
  "sure_casey_guilty \<longleftrightarrow>
      casey_elements_proved \<and>
      temporally_capable Casey_Lowe \<and>
      relevant_alternatives_excluded"

definition sure_jordan_guilty :: bool where
  "sure_jordan_guilty \<longleftrightarrow>
      jordan_elements_proved \<and>
      temporally_capable Jordan_Pike \<and>
      relevant_alternatives_excluded"

definition conviction_permitted :: "person \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "conviction_permitted p \<longleftrightarrow>
      (p = Morgan_Reed \<and> sure_morgan_guilty) \<or>
      (p = Casey_Lowe \<and> sure_casey_guilty) \<or>
      (p = Jordan_Pike \<and> sure_jordan_guilty)"

definition acquittal_required :: "person \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "acquittal_required p \<longleftrightarrow> \<not> conviction_permitted p"

theory Fuzzy_Temporal_Multi_Suspect_Investigation
  imports Complex_Main
begin

(* ============================================================ *)
(* Problem statement and definitions                            *)
(* ============================================================ *)

(*
  Entirely fictional case: The death of Dr Rowan Vale.

  Suspects:

    - Morgan Reed
    - Casey Lowe
    - Jordan Pike

  Possible time of the fatal injury:

    - 21:10
    - 21:15
    - 21:20

  This theory combines:

    - temporal reconstruction;
    - multiple suspects;
    - claimed and verified alibis;
    - fuzzy evidential degrees;
    - a comparative investigative score;
    - separate legal-proof conditions.

  Important distinction:

    "Most likely suspect" means only that one suspect receives the
    highest score under the expressly chosen investigative model.

    It does not mean:

      - that the suspect committed the offence;
      - that the evidence is legally sufficient;
      - that the prosecution has discharged its burden;
      - that a guilty verdict is permitted.

  The scoring weights are fictional modelling choices. They are not
  statements of forensic science or law.
*)

datatype person =
    Dr_Vale
  | Morgan_Reed
  | Casey_Lowe
  | Jordan_Pike
  | Unknown_Person

datatype timepoint =
    T2050
  | T2100
  | T2105
  | T2110
  | T2115
  | T2120
  | T2125
  | T2130
  | T2140
  | T2200

datatype location =
    Vale_Office
  | Office_Corridor
  | Northbridge_Library
  | Number_47_Bus
  | Central_Hospital
  | Unknown_Location

datatype exhibit =
    Knife_DNA
  | Knife_Fingerprint
  | Corridor_CCTV
  | Library_Access_Log
  | Library_CCTV
  | Bus_CCTV
  | Hospital_CCTV
  | Phone_Location_Data
  | Bloodstained_Jacket
  | Post_Mortem_Report

(*
  "proposition" is not used as an identifier.

  An investigative proposition is a limited factual claim that an
  exhibit or accepted reconstruction may support.
*)

datatype inv_proposition =
    Morgan_Handled_Knife
  | Casey_Handled_Knife
  | Jordan_Handled_Knife
  | Morgan_Was_Near_Scene
  | Casey_Was_Near_Scene
  | Jordan_Was_Near_Scene
  | Morgan_Wore_Jacket
  | Victim_Blood_On_Jacket
  | Morgan_Caused_Fatal_Injury
  | Casey_Caused_Fatal_Injury
  | Jordan_Caused_Fatal_Injury
  | Morgan_Had_Required_Intent
  | Casey_Had_Required_Intent
  | Jordan_Had_Required_Intent
  | Morgan_Acted_Unlawfully
  | Casey_Acted_Unlawfully
  | Jordan_Acted_Unlawfully

datatype alternative_explanation =
    Earlier_Innocent_Handling

*)

  Interpretation of the components:

  forensic_degree:
    Strength of accepted forensic evidence associating the suspect
    with relevant objects or materials.

  temporal_degree:
    Strength of accepted evidence placing the suspect in a position
    to commit the offence during the incident window.

  motive_degree:
    Strength of accepted evidence of a possible motive. Motive is
    neither necessary nor sufficient for guilt.

  conduct_degree:
    Strength of accepted post-event or surrounding conduct evidence.
    Ambiguous behaviour should receive a low degree.

  alternative_degree:
    Strength of realistic innocent or third-party explanations.

  alibi_degree:
    Strength and completeness of the suspect's alibi.

*)

definition residual_alternative_degree :: "person \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "residual_alternative_degree p = 100 - alternative_degree p"

definition residual_alibi_degree :: "person \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "residual_alibi_degree p = 100 - alibi_degree p"

  The investigative score gives greater weight to forensic and
  temporal evidence than to motive or conduct.

  Inculpatory components:

    forensic: 4
    temporal: 4
    motive:   1
    conduct:  1

  Exculpatory components are represented by residual values:

    absence of strong alternatives: 2
    absence of a strong alibi:      3

  Maximum total score:

    4\<times>100 + 4\<times>100 + 1\<times>100 + 1\<times>100 + 2\<times>100 + 3\<times>100

  an externally validated forensic or legal standard.
*)

definition investigative_score :: "person \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "investigative_score p =
      4 * forensic_degree p +
      4 * temporal_degree p +

      conduct_degree p +
      2 * residual_alternative_degree p +
      3 * residual_alibi_degree p"

definition normalised_score :: "person \<Rightarrow> real" where
  "normalised_score p =

theory Sqrt2_Irrational
  imports Main
begin

(* ========================================================================= *)
(* Problem/Puzzle Statement and Definitions                                  *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(*
  We describe a possible fraction representation of \<surd>2 using two
  natural numbers m and n.

  The usual mathematical argument turns the statement

      m / n = \<surd>2

  into the equation

      m² = 2n².

  We record only the resulting equation.
*)

definition has_factor_two :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "has_factor_two x \<longleftrightarrow> (\<exists>k::nat. x = 2 * k)"

definition simplified_fraction :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "simplified_fraction m n \<longleftrightarrow>
     \<not> (has_factor_two m \<and> has_factor_two n)"

definition sqrt_two_equation :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "sqrt_two_equation m n \<longleftrightarrow>
     n \<noteq> 0 \<and> m * m = 2 * (n * n)"

definition candidate_fraction :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "candidate_fraction m n \<longleftrightarrow>
     simplified_fraction m n \<and>
     sqrt_two_equation m n"

(*
  The novice does not know why the following facts are true.

  They simply accept what someone more experienced tells them:

    - the equation forces m to have a factor of 2
    - the equation forces n to have a factor of 2
*)

locale expert_facts =
  assumes first_number_has_factor_two:
    "\<And>m n::nat.
       m * m = 2 * (n * n)
       \<Longrightarrow> has_factor_two m"

  assumes second_number_has_factor_two:
    "\<And>m n::nat.
       m * m = 2 * (n * n)
       \<Longrightarrow> has_factor_two n"
begin

theory Thread_TimeClockwork
  imports Main
begin

(* thread:title Time puzzles · Again is not forever *)
(* thread:description I am reviewing a repeating clockwork gate. Instant 0: open, no chime. Instant 1: open, no chime. Instant 2: closed, no chime. After instant 2 the log returns to instant 0 and repeats. I must explain why recurring openings do not mean permanent opening, and why strong until fails. *)
(* thread:goal no_eventual_chime, until_fails, recurring_open, no_stable_open *)
(* This file contains only the problem assumptions and conditional dependency rules. *)
(* thread:reference {"title":"Promela reference: linear temporal logic","url":"https://spinroot.com/spin/Man/ltl.html","authors":"Spin project","year":"Reference manual","scope":"Semantics of always, eventually, next and strong until; the fictional trace puzzles are original."} *)
(* thread:label cycle_complete = The complete infinite cycle is open, open, closed, repeating from instant 0 *)
(* thread:label chime_absent = No release chime occurs in any stored instant or repeated cycle *)
(* thread:label closed_at_two = The gate is closed at instant 2 of every cycle *)
(* thread:label open_at_zero = The gate is open at instant 0 of every cycle *)
(* thread:label recurrence_semantics = G F open requires another open instant reachable from every instant *)
(* thread:label stability_semantics = F G open requires a suffix with no later closed instant *)
(* thread:label strong_until_semantics = Strong until requires an eventual right-condition witness and the left condition before that witness *)
(* thread:label eventual_semantics = F chime needs a chime witness in the present or future *)
(* thread:label no_eventual_chime = F chime is false because no chime occurs anywhere in the infinite cycle *)
(* thread:label until_fails = Open U chime is false because the required chime never occurs and the gate closes *)
(* thread:label recurring_open = G F open is true because each cycle supplies another opening from every instant *)
(* thread:label no_stable_open = F G open is false because every possible suffix has a later closed instant *)

locale Scenario =
  fixes cycle_complete chime_absent closed_at_two open_at_zero recurrence_semantics stability_semantics strong_until_semantics eventual_semantics no_eventual_chime until_fails recurring_open no_stable_open :: "bool"
  assumes cycle_complete_given: "cycle_complete"
      and chime_absent_given: "chime_absent"
      and closed_at_two_given: "closed_at_two"
      and open_at_zero_given: "open_at_zero"
      and recurrence_semantics_given: "recurrence_semantics"
      and stability_semantics_given: "stability_semantics"
      and strong_until_semantics_given: "strong_until_semantics"
      and eventual_semantics_given: "eventual_semantics"
      and no_event: "chime_absent & cycle_complete & eventual_semantics ==> no_eventual_chime"
      and until: "chime_absent & closed_at_two & strong_until_semantics ==> until_fails"
      and recur: "cycle_complete & open_at_zero & recurrence_semantics ==> recurring_open"
      and not_stable: "cycle_complete & closed_at_two & stability_semantics ==> no_stable_open"
begin
end

end

definitions: X p means p at the next instant. F p means p now or at some later instant. G p means p now and at every later instant.
p U q is strong until: q must occur, and p must hold strictly before its first occurrence. If q holds now, no earlier p is required.
G F p means p occurs again from every instant; F G p means that after some instant p never becomes false again.
Stored instants specify an infinite lasso: after the final instant the trace returns to the labelled loop start. Missing future evidence is never guessed.

queries.title: F chime: a release chime eventually sounds
open U chime: the gate stays open until a release chime occurs
G F open: from every instant the gate will open again
F G open: eventually the gate remains open forever

argumentation_concepts: Recurrence and stability: happening again is different from remaining true forever.
Strong until: the awaited event must actually occur, even when the initial condition holds.
Future coverage: I inspect the repeated loop rather than assuming a short prefix is complete.
